This article examines the characteristics of newly diagnosed adult patients at their first contact in the care pathway, serving as the baseline data for [[indikator-1a|Indikator 1a]] [^src1]. The dataset encompasses 2,406 patients in total, providing a comprehensive demographic and clinical profile of individuals entering the registry [^src1]. Because this analysis is based on a single reporting period, no longitudinal trends can be established.

In terms of clinical diagnoses, [[colitis-ulcerosa|Colitis ulcerosa]] is the clear leader, accounting for 1,494 patients (62%) [^src1]. [[crohns-sygdom|Crohns sygdom]] follows as the second most common condition with 905 patients (38%) [^src1]. [[psc|Primær skleroserende kolangitis (PSC)]] represents a very small fraction of the cohort with 7 patients (0%) [^src1], while [[korttarmssyndrom|korttarmssyndrom]] records no patients in this specific group [^src1]. 

The gender distribution is relatively balanced, showing a slight majority of women (1,252 or 52%) compared to men (1,154 or 48%) [^src1]. The average age of the cohort is 42 years (ranging from 17 to 93), with a median age of 39 years [^src1]. When analyzing the age groups, the 18-29 age bracket is the leader, comprising 736 patients (31%) [^src1]. Conversely, the oldest cohort, aged 90 or older, is the trailer with only 4 patients (0%) [^src1]. An interesting demographic outlier is the inclusion of 17 patients (1%) in the 0-17 years age group, which contrasts with the table's stated focus on adults ("voksne") [^src1].

Regarding healthcare utilization and contact patterns, patients had an average of 11 contacts (ranging from 1 to 41) and a median of 9 contacts [^src1]. Physical consultations lead the modality with 8,900 instances (65%), while virtual contacts account for 4,727 instances (35%) [^src1].
